questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
What does a production possibility curve show?

options.A: the maximum output that can be produced by a firm in a year
options.B: the maximum output that can be produced per worker per year in the economy
options.C: the maximum output that could be exported from a country
options.D: the maximum output of two or more goods in an economy from a given amount of inputs

questions.questionText: In Zimbabwe there was hyperinflation. Which two functions of money might the Zimbabwe dollar be most likely to have still performed during this hyperinflation?

options.A: medium of exchange and store of value
options.B: standard for deferred payments and unit of account
options.C: store of value and standard for deferred payments
options.D: unit of account and medium of exchange

questions.questionText: The diagram shows two production possibility curves, XX and YY. Y manufacturing X output O X Y agriculture output What would cause a movement from XX to YY?

options.A: a decrease in scarce resources
options.B: a decrease in the cost of resources
options.C: an increase in the cost of labour
options.D: an increase in the labour force

questions.questionText: The table shows the market demand and supply for bananas over a year. At a market price of 8 cents per kg there is disequilibrium in the market. total market total market price of bananas demand (million supply (million (cents per kg) tonnes) tonnes)
200 750 What action would the government have to take to achieve market equilibrium at a price of 8 cents per kg?

options.A: grant a subsidy of 2 cents per kg to producers
options.B: impose a tax of 4 cents per kg on consumers
options.C: purchase the entire supply at 8 cents and sell at 4 cents
options.D: ration consumers to 75kg each per year

What is price elasticity of supply?

options.A: the change in the quantity supplied when a price changes
options.B: the change in the quantity supplied when demand changes
options.C: the comparison of the proportionate change in supply to the proportionate change in demand
options.D: the comparison of the proportionate change in supply to the proportionate change in price

questions.questionText: In which situation is the demand for a product said to be price elastic?

options.A: A fall in price increases expenditure on the product.
options.B: A fall in price increases quantity demanded.
options.C: A rise in price increases expenditure on the product.
options.D: A rise in price reduces quantity demanded.

questions.questionText: Which product is most likely to be provided only by the government?

options.A: national defence
options.B: national health
options.C: national museums
options.D: national theatres

questions.questionText: Which term is given to an income received by an individual for which there is no corresponding contribution to output?

options.A: profit
options.B: revenue
options.C: salary
options.D: transfer payment

questions.questionText: A government policy favours older people at the expense of younger people. Which would be most likely to correct such an imbalance?

options.A: an increase in expenditure on government-provided pensions
options.B: an increase in government-subsidised training schemes for school-leavers
options.C: an increase in the rate of income tax on earned incomes
options.D: an increase in the rate of interest on savings

questions.questionText: A government gives a subsidy to a producer of a product. What will be the likely effect of this?

options.A: a shift to the left in the demand curve and a rise in equilibrium quantity
options.B: a shift to the left in the supply curve and a rise in equilibrium quantity
options.C: a shift to the right in the demand curve and a fall in equilibrium price
options.D: a shift to the right in the supply curve and a fall in equilibrium price

questions.questionText: Which is the most appropriate reason for the continued government ownership of a natural monopoly?

options.A: The government will guarantee competitive behaviour.
options.B: The government will ignore any losses made by the monopoly.
options.C: The government will maximise profits.
options.D: The government will take account of external benefits.

questions.questionText: When will the imposition of a tariff by a country on the goods and services of its major trading partners reduce the country’s expenditure on imports?

options.A: when the income elasticity of demand for imports is greater than 1
options.B: when the price elasticity of demand for imports is greater than 1
options.C: when the price elasticity of demand for imports is less than 1
options.D: when the price elasticity of supply of imports is greater than 1

questions.questionText: How will an increase in government spending on infrastructure affect aggregate demand and aggregate supply? aggregate demand aggregate supply

options.A: decreases increases
options.B: increases decreases
options.C: increases increases
options.D: stays the same increases

questions.questionText: The table shows the amount of good X or the amount of good Y that can be produced by country R and country T if each uses all of their resources. output of output of good X good Y country R 80 100 country T 20 80 What can be concluded from the table?

options.A: Country R has an absolute advantage in producing good Y and a comparative advantage in producing good X.
options.B: Country R has an absolute advantage in producing good X and a comparative advantage in producing good Y.
options.C: Country T has an absolute advantage in producing good X and a comparative advantage in producing good Y.
options.D: Country T has an absolute advantage in producing good Y and a comparative advantage in producing good X.

questions.questionText: What is most likely to lead to a persistent surplus in a country’s current account of its balance of payments?

options.A: a low domestic savings rate
options.B: an undervalued exchange rate
options.C: highly protectionist policies by other countries
options.D: low investment income from abroad

questions.questionText: What always happens when there is an increase in the Consumer Price Index?

options.A: an increase in consumer expenditure
options.B: an increase in the cost of living
options.C: a reduction in living standards
options.D: a reduction in real disposable income

questions.questionText: What would not be included in Germany’s balance of payments accounts?

options.A: financial investments in Germany by Japanese banks
options.B: foreign aid received by Germany
options.C: the German terms of trade
options.D: the takeover of a German company by a French company

questions.questionText: An economy has a balance of payments surplus, which it wishes to eliminate. In order to achieve this objective, which combination of polices would be most appropriate?

options.A: a depreciation of the currency and an increase in government spending
options.B: an appreciation of the currency and a cut in interest rates
options.C: an increase in the money supply and a pay freeze
options.D: increases in both direct and indirect taxation

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the possible relationships between the degree of independence of the central bank and the level of inflation. Which relationship suggests that central bank independence is an effective way to reduce inflation?

options.A: B annual inflation C rate D least most degree of central bank independence

questions.questionText: Which change in economic circumstances is most likely to lead to a reduction in the rate of domestic inflation in an economy?

options.A: a depreciation in the currency
options.B: a reduction in the productivity of labour
options.C: a world-wide recession
